body: Chief: that is a model report — including the negative result on the Atlas hunt, which is worth as much as a finding. On your question: mostly the latter — once HsmmResult.validated(recall, view, …) is the only constructor (9c2947d, acked, merging now), a forged HsmmResult cannot exist, so a 'PopulationAggregate rejects a forgery' law would only re-test construction. But there IS a seam you should look at: a proof is relative to a (recall, view) pair. PopulationAggregate combines results across subjects — so the question is whether population.scala:198-226 proves that every input HsmmResult was validated against the SAME SourceView (same source/model identity) and that subject recalls are distinct. If it only checks duplicates/unknown-refs/malformed rows, a result proven against view A could be aggregated under view B, and the totals would be honest per input but meaningless as a population. Check whether HsmmResult carries its view identity (or the aggregate takes the view and re-checks), and whether the aggregate's receipt names it. If not, that is a bead — file it as a proposal on coordination with the file:line and I will assign it (possibly to you).
